Full Name: ODD protocol (original) - Overview, Design concepts, and Details
Description: The original protocol for describing individual- and agent-based models, organised into three blocks (Overview; Design concepts; Details) and seven elements. Establishes a fixed narrative sequence so that readers can locate the same information in the same place across models.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Does not cover data provenance, calibration procedures, validation evidence, experimental design, or code archiving.
Binding Status: Voluntary (journal-encouraged in parts of ecology & JASSS)
Relationship to Other Entries: Superseded by SR-002 (ODD 2010) and SR-003 (ODD 2020); extended by SR-004, SR-005, SR-006
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Grimm, V., Berger, U., Bastiansen, F., Eliassen, S., Ginot, V., Giske, J., Goss-Custard, J., Grand, T., Heinz, S. K., Huse, G., Huth, A., Jepsen, J. U., Jørgensen, C., Mooij, W. M., Müller, B., Pe'er, G., Piou, C., Railsback, S. F., Robbins, A. M., ... DeAngelis, D. L. (2006). A standard protocol for describing individual-based and agent-based models. Ecological Modelling, 198(1-2), 115-126. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2006.04.023

Full Name: ODD protocol - review and first update
Description: First update to ODD, reorganising the seven elements and clarifying ambiguous guidance identified through five years of use.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: As SR-001: no data provenance, calibration, validation evidence or experiment design.
Relationship to Other Entries: Updates SR-001; superseded by SR-003
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Grimm, V., Berger, U., DeAngelis, D. L., Polhill, J. G., Giske, J., & Railsback, S. F. (2010). The ODD protocol: A review and first update. Ecological Modelling, 221(23), 2760-2768. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2010.08.019

Full Name: ODD protocol - second update
Description: Second update to ODD, sharpening guidance on replication and structural realism and clarifying the boundary between design concepts and implementation detail. The most widely used model-description standard in ABM.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Explicitly a model-description standard: does not specify how data were selected, how the model was calibrated, what validation was performed, or how experiments were designed.
Relationship to Other Entries: Updates SR-002; extended by SR-004 (ODD+D), SR-005 (ODD+P), SR-006 (ODD+2D)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Grimm, V., Railsback, S. F., Vincenot, C. E., Berger, U., Gallagher, C., DeAngelis, D. L., Edmonds, B., Ge, J., Giske, J., Groeneveld, J., Johnston, A. S. A., Milles, A., Nabe-Nielsen, J., Polhill, J. G., Radchuk, V., Rohwäder, M.-S., Stillman, R. A., Thiele, J. C., & Ayllón, D. (2020). The ODD protocol for describing agent-based and other simulation models: A second update to improve clarity, replication, and structural realism. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 23(2), 7. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.4259

Full Name: ODD+D - ODD for Decision making
Description: Extension adding a structured section for describing how agents decide: theoretical grounding, individual decision rules, learning, sensing, and the role of social norms.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Addresses decision-making description only; inherits all other ODD scope limits.
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends SR-002 / SR-003
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Müller, B., Bohn, F., Dreßler, G., Groeneveld, J., Klassert, C., Martin, R., Schlüter, M., Schulze, J., Weise, H., & Schwarz, N. (2013). Describing human decisions in agent-based models - ODD+D, an extension of the ODD protocol. Environmental Modelling & Software, 48, 37-48. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2013.06.003

Full Name: ODD+P - ODD complemented with Provenance information
Description: Extension attaching formal provenance records to an ODD description, so that each model element can be traced back to the data, assumption or prior model it derives from.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Provenance capture only; does not replace the ODD description itself.
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends SR-002 / SR-003; conceptually overlaps SR-011 (RAT-RS)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Reinhardt, O., Ruscheinski, A., & Uhrmacher, A. M. (2018). ODD+P: Complementing the ODD protocol with provenance information. In M. Rabe, A. A. Juan, N. Mustafee, A. Skoogh, S. Jain, & B. Johansson (Eds.), Proceedings of the 2018 Winter Simulation Conference (WSC) (pp. 727-738). IEEE. https://doi.org/10.1109/WSC.2018.8632481

Full Name: ODD+2D - ODD for Decision and Data
Description: Extension for mapping empirical data onto model entities and decision rules, adding an explicit data-to-model correspondence layer to the ODD structure.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Data mapping only; does not cover validation evidence or experiment design.
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends SR-002 / SR-003 and SR-004
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Laatabi, A., Marilleau, N., Nguyen-Huu, T., Hbid, H., & Babram, M. A. (2018). ODD+2D: An ODD based protocol for mapping data to empirical ABMs. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 21(2), 9. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.3646

Full Name: RAT-RS - Rigour And Transparency Reporting Standard
Description: Reporting standard for documenting data use in ABM. Structures reporting across data sources, model specification, calibration and validation, and handles qualitative, quantitative and mixed data on equal terms. Designed to complement, not replace, ODD.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Not a model-description standard; assumes a separate structural description (e.g. ODD).
GenAI / LLM Status: Pre-dates GenAI (LLM-assisted extraction trialled 2026, see EV-008)
Relationship to Other Entries: Complements SR-003; overlaps SR-005, SR-006
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Achter, S., Borit, M., Chattoe-Brown, E., & Siebers, P.-O. (2022). RAT-RS: A reporting standard for improving the documentation of data use in agent-based modelling. International Journal of Social Research Methodology, 25(4), 517-540. https://doi.org/10.1080/13645579.2022.2049511

Full Name: TRACE - TRAnsparent and Comprehensive model Evaludation
Description: Six-element documentation protocol (model description; data evaluation; conceptual model evaluation; implementation verification; model output verification; model analysis) covering the full 'evaludation' of a model. Produces a standalone supplementary document rather than in-text reporting. Concept proposed by Schmolke et al. (2010); standardised format established by Grimm et al. (2014).
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Assumes an existing model description (typically ODD) is embedded as element 1; heavy documentation burden reported as the main adoption barrier.
Binding Status: Effectively mandatory in some EU regulatory ecotoxicology submissions; voluntary elsewhere
Relationship to Other Entries: Embeds SR-003 as its first element; related to SR-024 (Sargent V&V)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Grimm, V., Augusiak, J., Focks, A., Frank, B. M., Gabsi, F., Johnston, A. S. A., Liu, C., Martin, B. T., Meli, M., Radchuk, V., Thorbek, P., & Railsback, S. F. (2014). Towards better modelling and decision support: Documenting model development, testing, and analysis using TRACE. Ecological Modelling, 280, 129-139. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ecolmodel.2014.01.018 | Concept originally proposed in: Schmolke, A., Thorbek, P., DeAngelis, D. L., & Grimm, V. (2010). Ecological models supporting environmental decision making: A strategy for the future. Trends in Ecology & Evolution, 25(8), 479-486. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tree.2010.05.001

Full Name: Pattern-Oriented Modelling
Description: Strategy for designing, parameterising and testing ABMs by requiring simultaneous reproduction of several observed patterns at different scales, so that model structure is constrained by multiple independent lines of evidence rather than a single fitted output.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: A design and testing strategy, not a reporting format; produces no standardised document.
Relationship to Other Entries: Complements SR-003; frequently paired with SR-012
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Grimm, V., Revilla, E., Berger, U., Jeltsch, F., Mooij, W. M., Railsback, S. F., Thulke, H.-H., Weiner, J., Wiegand, T., & DeAngelis, D. L. (2005). Pattern-oriented modeling of agent-based complex systems: Lessons from ecology. Science, 310(5750), 987-991. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1116681

Full Name: Docking / Model Alignment (model-to-model comparison)
Description: Cross-validation technique in which two independently built models of the same question are aligned and checked against each other, testing whether they produce equivalent results under equivalent conditions.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Requires a second independent implementation; rarely feasible in practice.
Relationship to Other Entries: Foundation for EV-003 (Edmonds & Hales) and EV-004 (Wilensky & Rand)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Axtell, R., Axelrod, R., Epstein, J. M., & Cohen, M. D. (1996). Aligning simulation models: A case study and results. Computational and Mathematical Organization Theory, 1(2), 123-141. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01299065

Full Name: A common protocol for agent-based social simulation
Description: Proposal for a procedural route by which the ABM community might agree a reporting standard, rather than a fixed documentation format itself.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Proposes a process, not a usable checklist or template.
Relationship to Other Entries: Historical precursor to SR-016 (Collins et al.)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Richiardi, M., Leombruni, R., Saam, N., & Sonnessa, M. (2006). A common protocol for agent-based social simulation. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 9(1), 15. https://www.jasss.org/9/1/15.html

Full Name: A Call to Arms: Standards for Agent-Based Modeling and Simulation
Description: Position paper arguing for adoption of existing and development of new descriptive, technical and software standards for ABM, reviewing ODD and UML-based options.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Advocacy; provides no checklist, template or schema.
Relationship to Other Entries: Argues for wider use of SR-003; NOTE: short reference collides with SR-041 (Collins et al. 2015b, TRIPOD) - disambiguated as 2015a/2015b
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Collins, A. J., Petty, M. D., Vernon-Bido, D., & Sherfey, S. J. (2015). A call to arms: Standards for agent-based modeling and simulation. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 18(3), 12. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.2838

Full Name: EABSS - Engineering Agent-Based Social Simulation
Description: Software-engineering approach to ABSS that produces a structured design document through a sequence of stakeholder-facing modelling steps (requirements, actors, use cases, agent state charts, validation plan).
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Design-stage focus; does not standardise reporting of results or data provenance.
Relationship to Other Entries: Base method for SR-022; conceptually related to SR-025 (Gaia)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Siebers, P.-O., & Klügl, F. (2017). What software engineering has to offer to agent-based social simulation. In B. Edmonds & R. Meyer (Eds.), Simulating social complexity (2nd ed., pp. 81-117). Springer.

Full Name: Conversational AI support for ABSS model design (EABSS + ChatGPT)
Description: Application of EABSS in which conversational AI prompt scripts support conceptualisation and generation of the design document, demonstrated on a museum adaptive-architecture case study. Released first as a CoMSES model/code entry, then as a peer-reviewed article.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Design stage only; does not address how AI involvement itself should be reported (see gap G-04).
Relationship to Other Entries: Applies SR-021 with GenAI support
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Siebers, P.-O. (2025). Exploring the potential of conversational AI support for agent-based social simulation model design. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 28(3), 2. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.5681 (Preprint: arXiv:2405.08032, 2024. Associated release: Siebers, P.-O. (2024). Engineering ABSS conceptualisation support using ChatGPT [Computational model]. CoMSES Computational Model Library.)

Full Name: MAIA - Modelling Agent systems via Institutional Analysis
Description: Framework translating institutional and social theory (based on Ostrom's IAD framework) into ABM elements via five structured conceptual views, for socio-technical system models.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Conceptualisation only; no reporting format for results or validation.
Machine-Readable: Partial (MAIA web tool generates structured model skeletons)
Relationship to Other Entries: Base framework for SR-026 (Ghorbani et al. 2015)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Ghorbani, A., Bots, P., Dignum, V., & Dijkema, G. (2013). MAIA: A framework for developing agent-based social simulations. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 16(2), 9. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.2166

Full Name: Verification and Validation of Simulation Models (Sargent framework)
Description: Reference framework distinguishing conceptual model validity, computerised model verification, operational validity and data validity, with a catalogue of V&V techniques (face validity, extreme-condition tests, sensitivity analysis, historical data validation, etc.).
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Provides a technique catalogue and vocabulary, not a reporting checklist - what gets reported is left open.
Binding Status: Voluntary; referenced in defence M&S VV&A policy
Relationship to Other Entries: Underpins validation elements of SR-012 and SR-031
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Sargent, R. G. (2013). Verification and validation of simulation models. Journal of Simulation, 7(1), 12-24. https://doi.org/10.1057/jos.2012.20

Full Name: Gaia Methodology for Agent-Oriented Analysis and Design
Description: Agent-oriented software engineering methodology treating multi-agent systems as computational organisations of interacting roles, covering macro-level (organisational) and micro-level (agent) design.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Engineered MAS focus; assumes designed rather than empirically grounded agents; no empirical validation guidance.
Relationship to Other Entries: Related to SR-021; from the MAS rather than social-simulation tradition
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Wooldridge, M., Jennings, N. R., & Kinny, D. (2000). The Gaia methodology for agent-oriented analysis and design. Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems, 3(3), 285-312. https://doi.org/10.1023/A:1010071910869

Full Name: Structuring Qualitative Data for Agent-Based Modelling
Description: Methodology for structuring and translating ethnographically collected qualitative data into ABM elements and outcome variables, building on MAIA.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Qualitative data only; no reporting template.
Relationship to Other Entries: Builds on SR-023; complements SR-011
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Ghorbani, A., Dijkema, G. P. J., & Schrauwen, N. (2015). Structuring qualitative data for agent-based modelling. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 18(1), 2. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.2573

Full Name: CAP - Characterisation and Parameterisation of human agents
Description: Framework of options for characterising and parameterising human agents in empirical ABMs, making explicit the choices involved in turning data into agent attributes and decision rules.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Agent characterisation only; does not address model structure or validation reporting.
Relationship to Other Entries: Complements SR-011 and SR-006
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Smajgl, A., & Barreteau, O. (2017). Framing options for characterising and parameterising human agents in empirical ABM. Environmental Modelling & Software, 93, 29-41. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2017.02.011

Full Name: DSG - Delineate, Structure and Gather
Description: Framework for structuring ABM data for social-ecological systems across three stages: delineating the system, structuring the data requirements, and gathering data.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Data-gathering focus; little uptake outside its originating context.
Relationship to Other Entries: Precursor to SR-011
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Altaweel, M. R., Alessa, L. N., Kliskey, A., & Bone, C. (2010). A framework to structure agent-based modeling data for social-ecological systems. Structure and Dynamics, 4(1). https://escholarship.org/uc/item/7kw1h48n

Full Name: MR POTATOHEAD conceptual design pattern framework
Description: Conceptual design pattern for documenting land-use/cover-change ABMs, decomposing a model into interchangeable components so that alternative models can be compared on a common frame.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Domain-specific to land-use change; not a general reporting format.
Relationship to Other Entries: Comparison-oriented alternative to SR-001
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Parker, D. C., Brown, D., Polhill, J. G., Manson, S., & Deadman, P. (2008). Illustrating a new 'conceptual design pattern' for agent-based models and land use via five case studies: The MR POTATOHEAD framework. In A. L. Paredes & C. H. Iglesias (Eds.), Agent based modelling in natural resource management. INSISOC.

Full Name: Dahlem ABM Documentation Guidelines
Description: Documentation guidelines for economic ABMs, written from a macroeconomics perspective and emphasising model equations, initialisation and parameter provenance.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Economics-oriented; limited uptake; no validation or experiment guidance.
Relationship to Other Entries: Domain alternative to SR-001/SR-003
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Wolf, S., Bouchaud, J.-P., Cecconi, F., Cincotti, S., Dawid, H., Gintis, H., van der Hoog, S., Jaeger, C. C., Kovalevsky, D. V., Mandel, A., & Paroussos, L. (2013). Describing economic agent-based models: Dahlem ABM documentation guidelines. Complexity Economics, 2(1), 63-74.

Full Name: FREIDA - FRamework for Expert-Informed Data-driven Agent-based models
Description: Mixed-methods framework for building, training and validating ABMs in data-sparse settings by formalising qualitative expert knowledge as Expected System Behaviours and combining it with quantitative data across the modelling cycle.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Preprint status; limited independent evaluation to date.
Relationship to Other Entries: Related to SR-013 (pattern-based constraint logic)
Verification Status: FIXED: preprint reference from LLM extension - author list incomplete ('et al.'), verify before citing
Reference (full): Oetker, F., Nespeca, V., Vis, T., Duijn, P., Sloot, P., & Quax, R. (2023). FREIDA: A framework for developing quantitative agent based models based on qualitative expert knowledge. arXiv:2308.00505. https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.00505

Full Name: Systematic Design of Experiments for simulation
Description: Approach to opening the 'black box' of simulation studies through systematic experimental design, factor screening and structured reporting of experimental setup and results.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Focused on simulated rather than empirical data; does not address model description or data provenance.
Relationship to Other Entries: Complements SR-003 (which omits experiment design); extended for DES by SR-043
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Lorscheid, I., Heine, B.-O., & Meyer, M. (2012). Opening the 'black box' of simulations: Increased transparency and effective communication through the systematic design of experiments. Computational and Mathematical Organization Theory, 18(1), 22-62. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10588-011-9097-3

Full Name: CRISP-DM-based methodology for assessing ABM outputs (with process mining)
Description: Adaptation of CRISP-DM combined with process mining to structure the assessment and documentation of agent-based simulation outputs and emergent behaviour.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Output-analysis focus; assumes the model itself is documented elsewhere.
Relationship to Other Entries: Adapts SR-061 (CRISP-DM)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Bemthuis, R. H., Govers, R. R., & Asadi, A. (2025). A CRISP-DM-based methodology for assessing agent-based simulation models using process mining. Journal of Simulation. https://doi.org/10.1080/17477778.2025.2508245 (Preprint: arXiv:2404.01114, 2024)

Full Name: Design of Experiments with Discrete-Event Simulation in OR: a review
Description: Review consolidating how DoE techniques should be selected, applied and reported alongside DES models in operational research, going beyond what STRESS specifies for experiments.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: DES-focused; recommendations not yet operationalised as a checklist.
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends the experiment-reporting elements of SR-051
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Gjerloev, A., Grieco, L., Lamé, G., & Crowe, S. (2025). Using design of experiments with discrete event simulation in operational research: A review. Journal of Simulation, 1-17. https://doi.org/10.1080/17477778.2025.2527151

Full Name: The Complexities of Agent-Based Modeling Output Analysis
Description: Community review of output-analysis practice in ABM, covering experimental design, sensitivity analysis, handling of stochasticity, replication counts and the reporting choices these imply.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Review rather than prescriptive standard; no checklist.
Relationship to Other Entries: Complements SR-041 and SR-045
Verification Status: Verified by expert
Reference (full): Lee, J.-S., Filatova, T., Ligmann-Zielinska, A., Hassani-Mahmooei, B., Stonedahl, F., Lorscheid, I., Voinov, A., Polhill, J. G., Sun, Z., & Parker, D. C. (2015). The complexities of agent-based modeling output analysis. Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 18(4), 4. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.2897

Full Name: Sensitivity analysis method selection for agent-based models
Description: Comparative guidance on which sensitivity analysis methods (OFAT, regression-based, variance-based/Sobol) suit which ABM analysis questions, and what must be reported for each to be interpretable.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Sensitivity analysis only.
Relationship to Other Entries: Operationalises part of SR-024 and SR-044
Verification Status: Verified by expert
Reference (full): ten Broeke, G., van Voorn, G., & Ligtenberg, A. (2016). Which sensitivity analysis method should I use for my agent-based model? Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation, 19(1), 5. https://doi.org/10.18564/jasss.2857

Full Name: STRESS - STrengthening the Reporting of Empirical Simulation Studies
Description: Reporting guideline family for empirical simulation studies in OR/management science, published as a parent paper with three method-specific 20-item checklists (ABS, DES, SD). Covers objectives, model logic, data, experimentation, implementation and code access.
Lifecycle Coverage: Operationalisation/Implementation; Data input & calibration; Experimentation; Dissemination/Archiving
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Validation is EXPLICITLY excluded from the guidelines.
Binding Status: Voluntary; endorsed by Journal of Simulation
Relationship to Other Entries: Parent of SR-052 (ABS), SR-053 (DES), SR-054 (SD) - all four entries share ONE publication; do not sum citation counts
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Monks, T., Currie, C. S. M., Onggo, B. S., Robinson, S., Kunc, M., & Taylor, S. J. E. (2019). Strengthening the reporting of empirical simulation studies: Introducing the STRESS guidelines. Journal of Simulation, 13(1), 55-67. https://doi.org/10.1080/17477778.2018.1442155

Full Name: STRESS-ABS - agent-based simulation checklist
Description: The 20-item STRESS checklist instantiated for agent-based simulation.
Lifecycle Coverage: Operationalisation/Implementation; Data input & calibration; Experimentation; Dissemination/Archiving
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Validation explicitly excluded (inherited from SR-051).
Relationship to Other Entries: Variant of SR-051 (same publication) - citation count is inherited, not independent
Citation Source & Date: Inherited from SR-051 - do not count separately
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): See SR-051 (same publication).

Full Name: STRESS-DES - discrete-event simulation checklist
Description: The 20-item STRESS checklist instantiated for discrete-event simulation.
Lifecycle Coverage: Operationalisation/Implementation; Data input & calibration; Experimentation; Dissemination/Archiving
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Validation explicitly excluded (inherited from SR-051).
Relationship to Other Entries: Variant of SR-051 (same publication) - citation count is inherited, not independent
Citation Source & Date: Inherited from SR-051 - do not count separately
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): See SR-051 (same publication).

Full Name: STRESS-SD - system dynamics checklist
Description: The 20-item STRESS checklist instantiated for system dynamics models.
Lifecycle Coverage: Operationalisation/Implementation; Data input & calibration; Experimentation; Dissemination/Archiving
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Validation explicitly excluded (inherited from SR-051).
Relationship to Other Entries: Variant of SR-051 (same publication) - citation count is inherited, not independent
Citation Source & Date: Inherited from SR-051 - do not count separately
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): See SR-051 (same publication).

Full Name: RGSR - Reporting Guidelines for Simulation-based Research in social sciences
Description: Reporting guidelines for simulation-based social science, separating requirements for reporting the model, the simulation experiments, and optimisation results. Distinguishes minimum from preferred reporting and specifies items such as number of iterations, convergence criteria, random seeds and computational cost. Motivated by an audit showing most System Dynamics Review papers were not reproducible.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Written around System Dynamics practice; agent-based specifics (agent heterogeneity, network structure) not covered.
Binding Status: Voluntary; influential on System Dynamics Review policy
Relationship to Other Entries: Precursor to SR-051; ABM analogue of SR-003 for experiment reporting
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): Rahmandad, H., & Sterman, J. D. (2012). Reporting guidelines for simulation-based research in social sciences. System Dynamics Review, 28(4), 396-411. https://doi.org/10.1002/sdr.1481

Full Name: ISPOR-SMDM Modeling Good Research Practices Task Force-4 (DES)
Description: Consensus guidance on structural development, parameter estimation, implementation, analysis and reporting for DES models used in health technology assessment.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Health technology assessment context; assumes a decision-analytic framing.
Binding Status: Effectively required by several HTA bodies for submitted models
Relationship to Other Entries: Health-economics counterpart to SR-051
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Karnon, J., Stahl, J., Brennan, A., Caro, J. J., Mar, J., & Möller, J. (2012). Modeling using discrete event simulation: A report of the ISPOR-SMDM Modeling Good Research Practices Task Force-4. Value in Health, 15(6), 821-827. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jval.2012.04.013

Full Name: MIASE - Minimum Information About a Simulation Experiment
Description: Minimum-information guideline for simulation experiments in systems biology: all components and settings must be listed and accessible, the simulation procedure described, and the handling of outputs specified. Implemented as the machine-readable SED-ML XML format, making it executable rather than merely narrative.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Developed for equation-based biological models; authors note applicability to wider modelling but agent-based specifics are not addressed.
Binding Status: Required by several systems-biology repositories; part of the COMBINE standards family
Relationship to Other Entries: Companion to SR-058 (MIRIAM); the machine-readable model that SR-003 lacks
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): Waltemath, D., Adams, R., Beard, D. A., Bergmann, F. T., Bhalla, U. S., Britten, R., Chelliah, V., Cooling, M. T., Cooper, J., Crampin, E. J., Garny, A., Hoops, S., Hucka, M., Hunter, P., Klipp, E., Laibe, C., Miller, A. K., Moraru, I., Nickerson, D., ... Le Novère, N. (2011). Minimum Information About a Simulation Experiment (MIASE). PLoS Computational Biology, 7(4), e1001122. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1001122

Full Name: MIRIAM - Minimum Information Requested In the Annotation of biochemical Models
Description: Rules specifying the information that must accompany an encoded model for it to be reused: provenance of the model, precise identification of every component via persistent identifiers, and the requirement that the model reproduce its published results when instantiated in a suitable simulator.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Assumes a formally encoded (SBML-like) model; not applicable to models that exist only as code.
Binding Status: Required for curated deposition in BioModels and similar repositories
Relationship to Other Entries: Companion to SR-057; part of the MIBBI/FAIRsharing minimum-information family
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): Le Novère, N., Finney, A., Hucka, M., Bhalla, U. S., Campagne, F., et al. (2005). Minimum information requested in the annotation of biochemical models (MIRIAM). Nature Biotechnology, 23(12), 1509-1515. https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt1156

Full Name: CRISP-DM - CRoss-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining
Description: Industry-independent six-phase process model for data mining projects: business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modelling, evaluation, deployment. The de facto process standard in applied data science.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: A process model, not a reporting standard: specifies phases, not what must be disclosed.
Relationship to Other Entries: Base standard adapted by SR-042
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Chapman, P., Clinton, J., Kerber, R., Khabaza, T., Reinartz, T., Shearer, C., & Wirth, R. (2000). CRISP-DM 1.0: Step-by-step data mining guide. The CRISP-DM Consortium.

Full Name: Datasheets for Datasets
Description: Standardised question set covering a dataset's motivation, composition, collection process, preprocessing, uses, distribution and maintenance, to be completed by dataset creators and read by dataset consumers.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Documents datasets, not models or modelling processes.
Binding Status: Voluntary; required by some ML conference tracks (e.g. NeurIPS D&B)
Relationship to Other Entries: Modernised as SR-065 (Open Datasheets); companion to SR-063
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Gebru, T., Morgenstern, J., Vecchione, B., Vaughan, J. W., Wallach, H., Daumé III, H., & Crawford, K. (2021). Datasheets for datasets. Communications of the ACM, 64(12), 86-92. https://doi.org/10.1145/3458723

Full Name: Model Cards for Model Reporting
Description: Short, modular reporting framework for trained ML models covering intended use, out-of-scope use, disaggregated performance across subgroups, training data, and ethical considerations.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Reports a trained artefact; does not document development process, data provenance or validation design.
Machine-Readable: Partial (widely emitted as Markdown on model hubs)
Binding Status: Voluntary; de facto required on major model hubs
Relationship to Other Entries: Closest existing analogue for a proposed 'ABM Card' (see gap G-05)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Mitchell, M., Wu, S., Zaldivar, A., Barnes, P., Vasserman, L., Hutchinson, B., Spitzer, E., Raji, I. D., & Gebru, T. (2019). Model cards for model reporting. In Proceedings of the Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT '19) (pp. 220-229). ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3287560.3287596

Full Name: Data Cards
Description: Transparency framework for dataset documentation at scale, organising content thematically across the dataset lifecycle and designed around the questions different stakeholder groups actually ask.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Dataset-level only.
Relationship to Other Entries: Successor-in-spirit to SR-062
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Pushkarna, M., Zaldivar, A., & Kjartansson, O. (2022). Data Cards: Purposeful and transparent dataset documentation for responsible AI. In Proceedings of the 2022 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency (FAccT '22) (pp. 1776-1826). ACM. https://doi.org/10.1145/3531146.3533231

Full Name: Open Datasheets - machine-readable dataset documentation
Description: Machine-readable (YAML/JSON) evolution of the datasheets approach, enabling automated validation and interoperable dataset documentation.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Preprint; adoption level unclear.
Relationship to Other Entries: Machine-readable form of SR-062
Verification Status: Verified by expert
Reference (full): Roman, A. C., Vaughan, J. W., See, V., Ballard, S., Torres, J., Robinson, C., & Ferres, J. M. L. (2023). Open Datasheets: A standardized, machine-readable format for dataset documentation. arXiv:2312.06153.

Full Name: FactSheets - Supplier's Declarations of Conformity for AI services
Description: Reporting framework documenting the performance, safety, security and provenance of AI models and services, framed as a supplier's declaration of conformity.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Service/product framing; assumes a supplier-consumer relationship not present in academic modelling.
Binding Status: Voluntary; influential on emerging AI conformity regimes
Relationship to Other Entries: Industry counterpart to SR-063
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Arnold, M., Bellamy, R. K. E., Hind, M., Houde, S., Mehta, S., Mojsilović, A., Nair, R., Ramamurthy, K. N., Olteanu, A., Piorkowski, D., Reimer, D., Richards, J., Tsay, J., & Varshney, K. R. (2019). FactSheets: Increasing trust in AI services through supplier's declarations of conformity. IBM Journal of Research and Development, 63(4/5), 6:1-6:13. https://doi.org/10.1147/JRD.2019.2942288

Full Name: REFORMS - Reporting Standards for Machine Learning Based Science
Description: Consensus-based, field-agnostic 32-item checklist for reporting ML-based scientific research, covering study goals, data, modelling, evaluation and claims. Developed in direct response to a documented wave of irreproducible ML-based findings across disciplines.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Predictive-modelling framing; explanatory/generative simulation is not its target.
Binding Status: Voluntary; endorsed by a large multidisciplinary author group
Relationship to Other Entries: Closest cross-domain analogue to a general ABM reporting standard
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Kapoor, S., Cantrell, E., Peng, K., Pham, T. H., Bail, C. A., Gundersen, O. E., Hofman, J. M., Hullman, J., Lones, M. A., Malik, M. M., Nanayakkara, P., Poldrack, R. A., Raji, I. D., Roberts, M., Salganik, M. J., Serra-Garcia, M., Stewart, B. M., Vandewiele, G., & Narayanan, A. (2024). REFORMS: Consensus-based recommendations for machine-learning-based science. Science Advances, 10(18), eadk3452. https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.adk3452

Full Name: FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship
Description: Four principles - Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable - for research data and metadata, emphasising machine-actionability. The reference point for most subsequent data-sharing policy.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Principles, not an implementation: deliberately silent on how to document a model's logic or its data use decisions. FAIR does not mean open.
Binding Status: Mandated by many funders (e.g. Horizon Europe, NIH DMS Policy) for data management plans
Relationship to Other Entries: Extended to software as SR-072
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Wilkinson, M. D., Dumontier, M., Aalbersberg, I. J., Appleton, G., Axton, M., Baak, A., et al. (2016). The FAIR Guiding Principles for scientific data management and stewardship. Scientific Data, 3, 160018. https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2016.18

Full Name: FAIR Principles for Research Software (FAIR4RS)
Description: Community-agreed adaptation of FAIR to research software, revising the principles to account for software's executability, composite nature and continuous versioning. Developed by a working group jointly convened by RDA, ReSA and FORCE11, engaging around 500 people.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Principles only; requires domain-specific implementation guidance (which ABM does not yet have).
Binding Status: Referenced in DFG, BMBF and other funder guidance
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends SR-071; directly applicable to ABM code deposited via SR-074
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (short): Barker et al. (2022) / Chue Hong et al. (2022)
Reference (full): Barker, M., Chue Hong, N. P., Katz, D. S., Lamprecht, A.-L., Martinez-Ortiz, C., Psomopoulos, F., Harrow, J., Castro, L. J., Gruenpeter, M., Martinez, P. A., & Honeyman, T. (2022). Introducing the FAIR Principles for research software. Scientific Data, 9, 622. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-022-01710-x | Principles themselves: Chue Hong, N. P., et al. (2022). FAIR Principles for Research Software version 1.0 (FAIR4RS Principles v1.0). Research Data Alliance. https://doi.org/10.15497/RDA00068

Full Name: TOP - Transparency and Openness Promotion Guidelines
Description: Modular journal-policy framework with eight standards (data citation; data, code and materials transparency; design and analysis reporting; study and analysis preregistration; replication) each at three tiers of stringency, from disclosure through requirement to independent verification. TOP 2025 reorganises the standards into Research Practices, Verification Practices and Verification Studies, with verifiability of empirical claims as the explicit objective.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Operates on journals, not on authors directly: it sets what a journal may require, not how a model should be described.
Machine-Readable: Partial (TOP Factor is a machine-comparable journal rating)
Binding Status: Adopted by 1,000+ journals; binding on authors wherever a journal has adopted Level 2 or 3
Relationship to Other Entries: The policy layer that would give SR-003 or SR-011 real force if a journal adopted them
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): Nosek, B. A., Alter, G., Banks, G. C., Borsboom, D., Bowman, S. D., Breckler, S. J., et al. (2015). Promoting an open research culture. Science, 348(6242), 1422-1425. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aab2374 | Update: Nosek, B. A., et al. (2026). TOP 2025: An update to the Transparency and Openness Promotion Guidelines. Research Integrity and Peer Review. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41073-026-00223-0

Full Name: CoMSES Net Computational Model Library
Description: Domain repository for ABM code and documentation with structured metadata, DOI assignment, versioning and an optional peer review of the model archive itself (checking that code runs and documentation is complete). The nearest thing social simulation has to a disciplinary deposit infrastructure.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Deposit is voluntary; archive peer review is opt-in; does not govern what appears in the article itself.
Binding Status: Voluntary; recommended by JASSS and some funders
Relationship to Other Entries: Practical deposit route for models documented with SR-003 / SR-011 / SR-012
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): Rollins, N. D., Barton, C. M., Bergin, S., Janssen, M. A., & Lee, A. (2014). A computational model library for publishing model documentation and code. Environmental Modelling & Software, 61, 59-64. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envsoft.2014.06.022

Full Name: AEA Data and Code Availability Policy; Data and Code Availability Standard (DCAS) v1.0
Description: Journal policy under which a paper cannot be published unless a complete replication package (data, code, README following a standard template, data availability statement with provenance) is deposited and independently verified by a dedicated Data Editor before acceptance. DCAS is the shared cross-journal standard the policy conforms to.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Verifies computational reproducibility of the submitted package; does not assess model description quality or validity.
Binding Status: MANDATORY for publication in all AEA journals; adopted in varying forms by Econometrica, ReStud, QJE, JPE
Relationship to Other Entries: The clearest example of an enforced, pre-publication reproducibility standard in the social sciences
Verification Status: Verified 2026-09-16 (web source)
Reference (full): American Economic Association. (2019, rev. 2024, 2026). Data and Code Availability Policy. https://www.aeaweb.org/journals/data/data-code-policy | Vilhuber, L., et al. Data and Code Availability Standard (DCAS) v1.0. https://datacodestandard.org/

Full Name: Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research
Description: Ten practical rules for computational reproducibility: record every step, avoid manual data manipulation, archive exact versions of external programs, version-control custom scripts, record intermediate results in standard formats, note random seeds, store raw data behind plots, connect textual claims to underlying results, and make all scripts and data publicly available.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Practice advice, not an auditable checklist or reporting format.
Relationship to Other Entries: Operational complement to SR-071 / SR-072
Verification Status: Added by expert review - verify before citing
Reference (full): Sandve, G. K., Nekrutenko, A., Taylor, J., & Hovig, E. (2013). Ten simple rules for reproducible computational research. PLoS Computational Biology, 9(10), e1003285. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285

Full Name: ACM Artifact Review and Badging
Description: Badging scheme in which independent reviewers assess research artefacts (code, data, environments) and award badges distinguishing artefacts that are available, functional/reusable, results reproduced, and results replicated. Introduces an agreed vocabulary separating repeatability, reproducibility and replicability.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Opt-in at most venues; assesses artefacts, not the scientific argument.
Binding Status: Voluntary at most ACM venues; mandatory artefact evaluation at some conferences
Relationship to Other Entries: Enforcement mechanism that could be applied to SR-074 deposits
Verification Status: Added by expert review - verify before citing
Reference (full): Association for Computing Machinery. (2020). Artifact Review and Badging - Current (Version 1.1). https://www.acm.org/publications/policies/artifact-review-and-badging-current

Full Name: Coupled Model Intercomparison Project experimental protocol (CMIP6)
Description: Community-wide experimental protocol prescribing a common set of simulation experiments, forcings, output variables, file formats and metadata that every participating climate model must produce. Compliance is the price of entry to the intercomparison and to the resulting assessment reports.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Assumes a mature community of comparable models; there is no ABM equivalent of a shared benchmark experiment set.
Binding Status: Effectively mandatory for participation in CMIP and for IPCC assessment inclusion
Relationship to Other Entries: The strongest cross-domain model for coordinated model comparison (cf. SR-014 Docking at single-pair scale)
Verification Status: Added by expert review - verify before citing
Reference (full): Eyring, V., Bony, S., Meehl, G. A., Senior, C. A., Stevens, B., Stouffer, R. J., & Taylor, K. E. (2016). Overview of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) experimental design and organization. Geoscientific Model Development, 9(5), 1937-1958. https://doi.org/10.5194/gmd-9-1937-2016

Full Name: EQUATOR Network
Description: International initiative and freely searchable library collating reporting guidelines across health research, with guidance on selecting and using them. Functions as the field's registry of standards rather than a standard itself.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Health research scope; simulation and computational modelling are barely represented.
Relationship to Other Entries: The institutional model this register is loosely modelled on (see blog post)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Simera, I., Moher, D., Hoey, J., Schulz, K. F., & Altman, D. G. (2010). A catalogue of reporting guidelines for health research. European Journal of Clinical Investigation, 40(1), 35-53. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2362.2009.02234.x

Full Name: CONSORT - Consolidated Standards of Reporting Trials
Description: Minimum reporting set for randomised controlled trials: 25-item checklist plus a participant flow diagram. The canonical example of a reporting guideline that became a de facto condition of publication.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: RCT-specific.
Binding Status: Required at submission by most major medical journals (ICMJE-aligned)
Relationship to Other Entries: Reference exemplar for SR-083 onward; extended by SPIRIT (SR-087) at protocol stage
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Schulz, K. F., Altman, D. G., & Moher, D. (2010). CONSORT 2010 statement: Updated guidelines for reporting parallel group randomised trials. BMJ, 340, c332. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.c332

Full Name: PRISMA - Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses
Description: 27-item checklist and flow diagram for reporting systematic reviews, covering search strategy, screening, eligibility, data extraction and synthesis.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Review methodology only.
Binding Status: Required by most health and many social science journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Directly applicable to systematic reviews of ABM literature
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Page, M. J., McKenzie, J. E., Bossuyt, P. M., Boutron, I., Hoffmann, T. C., Mulrow, C. D., et al. (2021). The PRISMA 2020 statement: An updated guideline for reporting systematic reviews. BMJ, 372, n71. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.n71

Full Name: STROBE - STrengthening the Reporting of OBservational studies in Epidemiology
Description: 22-item checklist for observational epidemiology covering cohort, case-control and cross-sectional designs.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Observational designs only.
Binding Status: Required or strongly encouraged by most epidemiology journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Extended for routinely collected data by SR-089 (RECORD)
Verification Status: Verified by expert
Reference (short): von Elm et al. (2007) + Vandenbroucke et al. (2007)
Reference (full): von Elm, E., Altman, D. G., Egger, M., Pocock, S. J., Gøtzsche, P. C., & Vandenbroucke, J. P. (2007). The Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE) statement: Guidelines for reporting observational studies. The Lancet, 370(9596), 1453-1457. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(07)61602-X. Vandenbroucke, J. P., Von Elm, E., Altman, D. G., Gøtzsche, P. C., Mulrow, C. D., Pocock, S. J., ... & Strobe Initiative. (2007). Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (STROBE): explanation and elaboration. PLoS medicine, 4(10), e297.

Full Name: ARRIVE - Animal Research: Reporting of In Vivo Experiments
Description: Checklist for reporting animal research, restructured in version 2.0 into an 'Essential 10' plus a recommended set.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: In vivo animal studies only.
Binding Status: Required by many journals and funders (e.g. NC3Rs-aligned)
Relationship to Other Entries: Example of a guideline restructured after evidence of poor compliance with v1
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Percie du Sert, N., Hurst, V., Ahluwalia, A., Alam, S., Avey, M. T., Baker, M., et al. (2020). The ARRIVE guidelines 2.0: Updated guidelines for reporting animal research. PLOS Biology, 18(7), e3000410. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3000410

Full Name: STARD - STAndards for Reporting Diagnostic accuracy studies
Description: 30-item checklist for studies evaluating diagnostic test accuracy.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Diagnostic accuracy studies only.
Binding Status: Required or encouraged by many clinical journals
Relationship to Other Entries: EQUATOR family (SR-081)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Bossuyt, P. M., Reitsma, J. B., Bruns, D. E., Gatsonis, C. A., Glasziou, P. P., Irwig, L., et al. (2015). STARD 2015: An updated list of essential items for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies. BMJ, 351, h5527. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.h5527

Full Name: SPIRIT - Standard Protocol Items: Recommendations for Interventional Trials
Description: Checklist of items for a clinical trial PROTOCOL - i.e. reporting standards applied before the study is run, not after. The protocol-stage counterpart to CONSORT.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Protocol stage only.
Binding Status: Required by many funders and ethics committees
Relationship to Other Entries: Protocol-stage analogue that ABM currently lacks entirely (see gap G-06); pairs with SR-082
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Chan, A.-W., Tetzlaff, J. M., Altman, D. G., Laupacis, A., Gøtzsche, P. C., Krleža-Jerić, K., et al. (2013). SPIRIT 2013 statement: Defining standard protocol items for clinical trials. Annals of Internal Medicine, 158(3), 200-207. https://doi.org/10.7326/0003-4819-158-3-201302050-00583

Full Name: TRIPOD - Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model
Description: Reporting guideline for studies developing, validating or updating a multivariable prediction model. Notable for treating the MODEL, rather than the study design, as the reported object - the closest medical analogue to reporting a simulation model.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Predictive (not explanatory/generative) models.
Binding Status: Required or encouraged by many clinical journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Extended as SR-090; NOTE: short reference collides with SR-016 - disambiguated as Collins et al. (2015b)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Collins, G. S., Reitsma, J. B., Altman, D. G., & Moons, K. G. M. (2015). Transparent reporting of a multivariable prediction model for individual prognosis or diagnosis (TRIPOD): The TRIPOD statement. BMJ, 350, g7594. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.g7594

Full Name: RECORD - REporting of studies Conducted using Observational Routinely-collected health Data
Description: STROBE extension adding items on the provenance, linkage, cleaning and coding of routinely collected data - i.e. a data-use reporting layer bolted onto an existing design standard.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Routinely collected health data only.
Binding Status: Required or encouraged by several journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Structural analogue of RAT-RS (SR-011) relative to ODD (SR-003): a data-use extension to a description standard
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Benchimol, E. I., Smeeth, L., Guttmann, A., Harron, K., Moher, D., Petersen, I., et al. (2015). The REporting of studies Conducted using Observational Routinely-collected health Data (RECORD) statement. PLOS Medicine, 12(10), e1001885. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001885

Full Name: TRIPOD+AI
Description: Extension of TRIPOD covering clinical prediction models built with regression or machine learning, adding items on data preparation, model specification, computational reproducibility and code availability.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Clinical prediction context.
Binding Status: Required or encouraged by BMJ and allied journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Extends SR-088; example of an established standard successfully retro-fitted for AI (a route open to ODD)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Collins, G. S., Moons, K. G. M., Dhiman, P., Riley, R. D., Beam, A. L., Van Calster, B., et al. (2024). TRIPOD+AI statement: Updated guidance for reporting clinical prediction models that use regression or machine learning methods. BMJ, 385, e078378. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-078378

Full Name: CHEERS - Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards
Description: Reporting checklist for health economic evaluations, including model-based analyses - covering model structure, assumptions, parameter sources and uncertainty analysis.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Economic evaluation framing; model structure reporting is comparatively thin.
Binding Status: Required by most health economics journals
Relationship to Other Entries: Relevant precedent: a reporting standard that covers decision-analytic MODELS
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Husereau, D., Drummond, M., Augustovski, F., de Bekker-Grob, E., Briggs, A. H., Carswell, C., et al. (2022). Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards 2022 (CHEERS 2022) statement. BMJ, 376, e067975. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2021-067975

Full Name: MOOSE - Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology
Description: Reporting checklist for meta-analyses of observational studies.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Observational meta-analysis only; largely superseded in practice by PRISMA.
Relationship to Other Entries: EQUATOR family (SR-081); overlaps SR-083
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Stroup, D. F., Berlin, J. A., Morton, S. C., Olkin, I., Williamson, G. D., Rennie, D., et al. (2000). Meta-analysis of observational studies in epidemiology: A proposal for reporting. JAMA, 283(15), 2008-2012. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.283.15.2008

Full Name: CARE - CAse REport guidelines
Description: Consensus checklist for reporting clinical case reports.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Single-case clinical reports; limited transferability to modelling.
Relationship to Other Entries: EQUATOR family (SR-081)
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Gagnier, J. J., Kienle, G., Altman, D. G., Moher, D., Sox, H., & Riley, D. (2013). The CARE guidelines: Consensus-based clinical case reporting guideline development. Headache, 53(10), 1541-1547. https://doi.org/10.1111/head.12246

Full Name: SRQR - Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research
Description: 21-item reporting guideline for qualitative research designs, covering researcher reflexivity, sampling, data collection, analysis and trustworthiness - the dimensions a quantitative checklist has no vocabulary for.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Qualitative empirical research; not written for models that consume qualitative data.
Relationship to Other Entries: Directly relevant to the qualitative-data half of SR-011 and SR-026
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): O'Brien, B. C., Harris, I. B., Beckman, T. J., Reed, D. A., & Cook, D. A. (2014). Standards for reporting qualitative research: A synthesis of recommendations. Academic Medicine, 89(9), 1245-1251. https://doi.org/10.1097/ACM.0000000000000388

Full Name: SQUIRE - Standards for QUality Improvement Reporting Excellence
Description: Reporting guideline for healthcare quality improvement work, notable for requiring explicit statement of the programme theory and of how context shaped the intervention.
Explicit Exclusions / Scope Limits: Healthcare improvement context.
Relationship to Other Entries: Programme-theory requirement is a useful precedent for reporting ABM mechanisms
Verification Status: Carried over from v0.2 - NOT independently verified
Reference (full): Ogrinc, G., Davies, L., Goodman, D., Batalden, P., Davidoff, F., & Stevens, D. (2016). SQUIRE 2.0 (Standards for QUality Improvement Reporting Excellence): Revised publication guidelines from a detailed consensus process. BMJ Quality & Safety, 25(12), 986-992. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjqs-2015-004411
